title: Per-epoch position resampling: expose all ~45k Berlin train vantages instead of a frozen 6k subset
hypothesis: The champion's 810 m is limited by training-set exposure, not by its (validated) grid-classification architecture. train.py's load_training_plan picks 6,000 crop positions ONCE and reuses them for all 96 epochs — only the rotation is refreshed. The frozen split (pipeline/dataset.py) documents ~45k available train positions for a ~7 km area, so the model literally never sees ~87% of its own training territory: of the grid cells that contain at least one train position, a fixed 6k draw leaves hundreds with zero positives for the entire run, and the cells it does cover average only ~2 fixed vantage points memorized 96 times over. That is exactly the label starvation experiment 4 diagnosed — but exp 4 attacked it by reparameterizing the decode head (coarse cells + offsets), which was refuted at 920 m. This experiment attacks the same bottleneck directly in the training procedure, with the architecture untouched: redraw the 6,000 positions at random from the full ~45k train list before every epoch. At unchanged per-epoch cost (extraction time scales with count, not novelty; ~3.3 s/epoch measured), 96 epochs then cover essentially every trainable position (P(a position is never drawn) ≈ 0.867^96 ≈ 1e-6), turning the long budget into dataset-scale coverage instead of repetition — every populated cell gets positives, and lookalike cells get far more distinct negatives to discriminate against. (Note: this is the third attempt at iteration 5 — the same design was pre-registered twice before but never reached a score; both prior attempts died to harness interruptions, not to any result. It is re-registered here after independently re-verifying its claims against the current champion code.)
method: model/train.py only: move training-plan sampling inside the epoch loop so each epoch draws a fresh random 6,000 positions (with fresh rotations, as now) from the full train-split crop list, instead of freezing one 6,000-position plan for the whole run. model/model.py untouched — identical architecture, loss, and ONNX export.
expected_outcome: Worst-case median error (the single Berlin/asis cell) drops from 810 m into the 450–700 m range: distinct training images rise ~7.5x (6k -> ~45k, each still freshly rotated), which should sharpen cell discrimination among Berlin lookalikes — the current dominant error mode, since 810 m ≈ 7.5 cells is far beyond the ~2-cell floor imposed by never-trained eval-block interiors. Any score under ~750 m supports the direction. If the metric does NOT improve despite 7.5x more distinct data, training-data quantity is cleanly exonerated and the feature extractor / decode is indicted — pointing the next experiment at pretrained init or descriptor design with real information. Known residual (not claimed fixed): cells inside eval blocks still receive zero positives — that is structural to the frozen split and unchanged here. Coverage-gate risk is low: more diverse data may soften train-set fit, but the champion's coverage is 0.545 vs the 0.2 gate, and better generalization typically raises eval-time confidence on unseen crops. Deployment gates identical by construction (same ONNX graph: ~2.5 MiB, 0.63 ms host proxy). Wall-time unchanged, ~10–15 min on MPS.
eli5: The model has been studying the same 6,000 flashcards over and over — 96 study sessions with the exact same deck — when the full deck of Berlin views actually has 45,000 cards. We now deal a fresh random hand of 6,000 cards before every study session. Same total study time, same brain, but by the end it has seen essentially every card in the deck a few times instead of 13% of them dozens of times. Seeing far more of Berlin should make it much better at telling apart neighborhoods that look confusingly similar.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: Small 4-layer CNN that shrinks the image step by step into a 128-number summary of what the ground below looks like

stages.name: Map-grid classifier
stages.detail: Scores all 4096 squares of a 64×64 checkerboard laid over Berlin: 'how much does this frame look like each square?'

stages.name: Coordinate + confidence readout
stages.detail: Averages the highest-scoring squares into one precise (lat, lon) point; confidence = how much belief lands in one small neighborhood of the map

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: Same multiple-choice loss and 96 passes, but the 6,000 training photos are re-drawn at random from all ~45,000 mapped spots before every pass — by the end the model has seen essentially every trainable spot in Berlin, instead of the same 13% over and over

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py must not change in any way (same TinyLocNet, GRID=64, loss_fn, export_onnx) — the exported ONNX graph must be identical in structure to the champion's.

FIXED CONTRACTS (do not break): (1) CLI: python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir <d>] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N] [--seed N] — the harness calls it exactly like this with --epochs 8 and --max-crops-per-bucket 6000. (2) ONNX export contract per model/model.py docstring: one ONNX per area at <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx, input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalized map coords, conf in [0,1]. (3) train_info.json append behavior in main() stays as-is. (4) EPOCH_MULT=12, Adam lr 1e-3, CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=total_epochs, eta_min=1e-5), batch size 64, torch.manual_seed(seed) + np.random.default_rng(seed), and the device selection logic all stay exactly as they are.

THE ONE CHANGE — per-epoch position resampling in train.py:

1. Replace load_training_plan(area, data_dir, max_crops_per_bucket, rng) with a loader that does NOT sample: load_area_assets(area, data_dir) -> (meta, buckets, crops) where buckets is the list of (bucket_name, img ndarray) for each entry in LIGHTING_BUCKETS (load each relight/<bucket>.png once, before the epoch loop — never per epoch) and crops = list_crops(area, meta["width"], meta["height"], "train") (the full list, ~45k for Berlin).

2. Add sample_epoch_plan(buckets, crops, meta, max_crops_per_bucket, rng) -> (plan, y): for each bucket image, picks = rng.choice(len(crops), size=min(max_crops_per_bucket, len(crops)), replace=False), then plan entries (img, cx, cy) and targets crop_center_norm(meta, cx, cy) exactly as the old loader built them; y = torch.tensor(ys, dtype=torch.float32). This is called INSIDE the epoch loop, once per epoch, BEFORE building the epoch tensor, using the same rng that already drives rotations (order of rng calls may differ from the champion — that is fine, no reproducibility contract across experiments).

3. In train_area's epoch loop: each epoch, (plan, y) = sample_epoch_plan(...), then x = epoch_tensor(plan, rng) (keep epoch_tensor unchanged — fresh random rotation per crop). Batch loop then indexes x and THIS EPOCH'S y (y is no longer loop-invariant — make sure the minibatch targets come from the current epoch's y). n = len(plan) per epoch (will be constant at bucket_count * 6000, but read it per epoch anyway).

4. Fallback path (EXTRACT_BUDGET_S): keep the guard. If an epoch's extraction time exceeds EXTRACT_BUDGET_S, degrade gracefully to the champion's old behavior from that point on: freeze the CURRENT epoch's plan and y, build the ROT_POOL rotation pool from that frozen plan (build_rot_pool unchanged), and use epoch_tensor_from_pool for all remaining epochs (no further position resampling). Measured extraction on the target machine is ~3.3 s for 6,000 crops, so this path should never trigger there — it exists for slower environments only.

5. Logging: in the returned info dict, keep every existing key (n_train_crops = per-epoch crop count, epochs, harness_epochs, epoch_mult, device, train_seconds, onnx_bytes, init: "from-scratch") and ADD "position_sampling": "per-epoch" and "distinct_positions_available": len(crops). Update the module docstring's description of the sampling strategy to match (selection is now per-epoch, not fixed once).

Everything else in train.py — _to_tensor, epoch_tensor, build_rot_pool, epoch_tensor_from_pool, export at the end of train_area, main() — stays untouched except as required by points 1–4.
